settings.heading: Claude Code is powerful. The hard part is knowing what to tell it.
settings.intro: The bottleneck was never the model's ability to write code. It is that most people have no repeatable process for directing it.

settings.title: Vague instructions, inconsistent results
settings.body: “Build me a website” produces a website — a different one every time. Nothing about the second attempt learns from the first.

settings.title: Architecture drifts between sessions
settings.body: Every session starts with a blank context window. By session five you have three form patterns, two CSS strategies, and a utility function written four times.

settings.title: SEO gets bolted on afterwards
settings.body: URL structure, canonicals, and metadata are decided implicitly by whatever got built first. Fixing them later means redirects and lost ground.

settings.title: Security is remembered too late
settings.body: AI-assisted development produces .env files and hardcoded test keys with real enthusiasm. Finding them after the first push means rotation, not deletion.

settings.title: Deployment is improvised
settings.body: No pipeline, no preview, no rollback. The first bad deploy is the one that teaches you why those exist.

settings.title: Nobody defined what done means
settings.body: Without stated completion criteria, “done” is whatever the model decides it is when it stops writing.

settings.heading: One prompt, or one process
settings.intro: Both of these run in the same tool. Only one of them produces something you can put in front of customers.

settings.heading: What the prompts actually look like
settings.intro: Short excerpts from four of the 67 prompt documents. Each full prompt runs to several pages and carries its own objective, variables, role, instructions, constraints, validation, deliverables, and completion criteria.
settings.footnote: The constraints and completion criteria do most of the work: they define what done means before Claude starts, so done is not something the model gets to decide afterwards.

settings.excerpt:
Analyse this repository. Do not modify anything.

Map: structure, stack, entry points, data,
configuration, conventions in force, tests.

Cite file paths for every claim. If you could
not determine something, say so rather than
guessing.

  …

Every finding needs evidence. Quote the file,
the URL, the header, the response.

Never invent metrics. No search volumes, no
difficulty scores, no traffic estimates.
Say "not measured".

State your blind spots.

  …

Check the full git history, all branches and
tags — a secret removed in a later commit is
still in history and still compromised.

Rotate the credential FIRST. Removing it from
the repository does not un-expose it.

  …

Never use fabricated testimonials, invented
customer counts, countdown timers with no real
deadline, or crossed-out prices never charged.

These are not aggressive marketing. They are
deception, and customers find out.

  …

settings.heading: Built for people shipping real work
settings.intro: Technically intermediate to highly technical. You do not need to be a professional developer — but you do need to be willing to read what Claude produces and push back when it is wrong.

settings.question: Do I need Claude Code?
settings.answer: Yes. This is a system for directing Claude Code, and it does nothing on its own.

settings.question: Is a paid Claude plan required?
settings.answer: Per Anthropic's current documentation, Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account — the free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code access. It can also run against Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Anthropic changes plans and features regularly, so check code.claude.com/docs before relying on this.

settings.question: Do I need to know how to code?
settings.answer: Not professionally. You do need to be comfortable in a terminal and willing to read what Claude produces and push back when it is wrong — the whole system is built around that habit. If you will not review the output, this will not help you.

settings.question: Does it work with an existing website?
settings.answer: Yes. There is a dedicated audit prompt for existing sites, a rescue prompt for broken or compromised ones, and a redesign prompt built around not losing the traffic you already have.

settings.question: Which platforms does it cover?
settings.answer: Dedicated build systems for Shopify, WordPress, Astro, SaaS applications, and landing pages. The master prompt and the security, accessibility, SEO, and checklist material are platform-agnostic. It is not a claim of universal compatibility with every framework.

settings.question: Will this guarantee rankings, traffic, or revenue?
settings.answer: No, and anyone promising that is selling something that does not exist. This is a professional system for directing Claude Code through planning, development, optimisation, deployment, and launch. Search engines decide what to index and rank; customers decide what to buy.

settings.title: Set the project context first
settings.body: Module 02 is the step people skip. A CLAUDE.md that states the commands, the boundaries and the definition of done, before a single prompt is run.

settings.title: Run the master prompt
settings.body: Open Claude Code in the project and paste the master prompt for your situation. It runs as staged work, not one wish.
settings.code:
$ claude

> Read 01-Master-System/MASTER-WEBSITE-BUILDER-PROMPT.md
> and work through it stage by stage. Stop at the end of
> each stage and show me what you have.

settings.title: Thirteen stages, in dependency order
settings.body: The workflow is ordered so each stage can be checked before the next one depends on it. Skipping ahead is how a build becomes unverifiable.
settings.code:
Research → Plan → Architect → Design → Build → Write
 → Optimize → Secure → Test → Deploy → Index
 → Monitor → Improve

settings.heading: What are you trying to build?
settings.intro: Three questions, then a seven-step route through the free guides for exactly that job. Tick steps off as you go — your progress is saved in this browser, with no account.

settings.body: Planning, platform build systems, a production CLAUDE.md, security, accessibility, Git, deployment and launch checklists. The whole lifecycle, from nothing to live.
Crawlability, indexation, structured data, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, Search Console and content auditing. For a site that exists and is not ranking.
Funnels, page audits, forms, analytics, experimentation and conversion copy. For traffic that already arrives and does not turn into revenue.
Monitoring, security checks, backups, dependency updates, deployment gates, incident playbooks and monthly reporting. For a site that is live and has to stay that way.
